items.q: Commonest cause of congenital stridor beginning in first weeks, worse supine, better prone, is what?
items.exp: Supraglottic floppiness prolapses on inspiration in neonates, feeding or reflux aggravated, resolving as airway matures by about two years in most. Cord palsy weakens cry with aspiration pattern instead.
r: Incorrect. Stenosis is fixed biphasic noise after intubation often.

items.q: Three year old at midnight with seal bark cough, stridor, low grade fever, responds to steroid. Diagnosis and airway X ray sign?
o: Viral croup (laryngotracheitis); steeple sign subglottic narrowing
items.exp: Parainfluenza croup oedematises subglottis (steeple on AP neck film, imaging rarely needed) causing bark and stridor; dexamethasone reduces severity and returns, adrenaline buys time in severe obstruction.
r: Incorrect. Epiglottitis drools toxic without bark.
Incorrect. Foreign body sudden afebrile choking.

items.q: Toxic drooling 4 year old sitting forward, thumbprint epiglottis suspected. Immediate rule is what?
o: Do not instrument throat; assemble ENT anaesthesia in theatre for controlled intubation
items.exp: Epiglottic swelling can completely obstruct with distress or instrumentation; child stays with parent, minimal upset, theatre team secures airway under inhalational anaesthesia with surgical backup, then IV antibiotics (Hib cover patterns).
r: Correct. Theatre controlled airway, hands off throat.
Incorrect. Ward nebuliser delays definitive airway.
items.kp: Drooling tripod: theatre tube, no peeking.

items.q: Nebulised adrenaline in severe croup provides what benefit and limitation?
o: Temporary (about 2 hours) obstruction relief, needs steroid cover and observation for rebound
items.exp: Vasoconstriction shrinks subglottic oedema briefly (onset minutes, waning by two hours) bridging steroid effect; discharge waits observation after last dose per local policy. It never secures epiglottitis airway.
r: Correct. Two hour bridge with steroid.
items.kp: Adrenaline buys two hours in croup.

items.q: Sudden stridor and unilateral reduced air entry after toddler choked on peanut at party needs what?
o: Rigid bronchoscopy for inhaled foreign body removal
items.exp: Organic foreign bodies (peanut oils inflame) lodge bronchus (right more vertical) or larynx causing ball valve signs; bronchoscopy diagnoses and removes, imaging may show air trapping but normal film does not exclude.
r: Incorrect. Delay infects and swells object.
Incorrect. Afebrile sudden onset not croup.
Incorrect. Asymptomatic intervals still harbour object.
items.kp: Choked toddler, one quiet lung: scope it out.

items.q: Bilateral vocal cord palsy in neonate most characteristically presents how and associates with what?
o: Stridor with weak cry and aspiration, central causes like Chiari malformation or birth injury
items.exp: Both cords near midline obstruct airway (stridor, possible tracheostomy) while unilateral palsy weakens cry and aspirates; bilateral neonatal cases need brain and Chiari evaluation (Arnold Chiari II with myelomeningocele classic).
r: Correct. Bilateral palsy stridor, central hunt.
Incorrect. Feeding noise alone is malacia pattern.
Incorrect. Teen hoarseness is functional or papilloma.
items.kp: Both cords frozen in baby: check brain stem causes.

items.q: Unilateral vocal cord palsy after thyroidectomy in adult mainly causes what?
o: Breathy hoarseness, weak cough and aspiration risk, usually airway adequate
items.exp: One paramedian cord leaves glottic gap wasting air and protection; speech therapy, temporary injection medialisation or thyroplasty restores voice and swallow, while bilateral palsy threatens airway instead.
items.kp: One cord out: breathy. Two out: airway.

items.q: Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis causing progressive hoarseness and stridor in child is driven by which virus and birth link?
o: HPV 6 and 11, often vertical exposure at vaginal delivery in juvenile onset
items.exp: Low risk HPV types grow exophytic laryngeal papillomas needing repeated surgical debulking preserving voice, adjuvant therapies in aggressive disease, HPV vaccination prevention shifting epidemiology.
r: Incorrect. EBV drives nasopharynx and mono.
items.kp: Warty voice box in child: HPV six eleven.

items.q: Subglottic stenosis in child is most often acquired from what and sounds how?
o: Prolonged neonatal intubation injury; fixed biphasic stridor
items.exp: Cricoid subglottis is narrowest fixed ring; endotracheal pressure scars it circumferentially causing biphasic noise and croup that fails to resolve, graded Cotton Meyer for airway surgery decisions.
r: Correct. Intubation scar, biphasic fixed stridor.
Incorrect. Reflux aggravates, rarely sole cause.
Incorrect. Measles caused historical croup deaths, not stenosis pattern.
items.kp: Tube scar at cricoid narrows both breath phases.

items.q: Steeple sign versus thumbprint sign on neck imaging belong to which pair in order?
o: Croup subglottic steeple; epiglottitis swollen epiglottis thumbprint
items.exp: AP film in croup tapers subglottis to steeple (church spire), lateral film in epiglottitis shows thumb sized epiglottis; imaging never delays airway care in unstable children.
